label: Abort the journey
summary: Stops a travel plan at once.
details: No further travelling happens. The game then runs the on_action `on_travel_plan_abort`. Runs on a travel plan, and vanilla only ever writes `yes`.

label: Accept activity invite
summary: Makes the character accept an invitation to the given activity.
details: The character uses their default travel plan for it. Runs on a character; the value is the activity.

label: Accept invite, no travel
summary: Makes the character accept an invitation to the given activity without giving them a travel plan.
details: The character must already be at the activity's location, otherwise they are kicked out of the activity. Runs on a character; the value is the activity.

label: Accept task contract
summary: Going by its name, makes the character accept the given task contract; the game documents nothing more.
details: The game's documentation gives only the syntax, so the exact consequences are not stated. Vanilla passes a saved task contract, for example `scope:contract`. Runs on a character.

label: Activate a catalyst
summary: Activates a catalyst of a struggle.
details: Runs on a struggle. The short form is just the catalyst name. The long form can also name a character; vanilla mostly uses the long form.

fields.name: catalyst
fields.text: Which catalyst to activate.

fields.name: character
fields.text: A character tied to the catalyst (the app asks "Caused by whom?"). Vanilla passes actors such as `root`, `scope:attacker` or `scope:defender`.
fields.values: a character, for example `root` or a saved scope

label: Add a log entry
summary: Adds an entry to the log of an activity.
details: Runs on an activity. Vanilla always gives a text key and a character. The score is a script value; vanilla uses values such as 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100. If the location is left out, the activity's current location is used. If `show_in_conclusion` is left out, it is `no`.

fields.name: key
fields.text: The localization key of the entry's text.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the entry is about.

fields.name: score
fields.text: The points the entry is worth.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: tags
fields.text: Labels attached to the entry; vanilla uses words like `good`, `bad` and `contest`.
fields.values: a list of words in braces

fields.name: show_in_conclusion
fields.text: Whether the entry is shown in the activity's conclusion.

fields.name: target
fields.text: A second character the entry involves.

fields.name: location
fields.text: The province the entry is tied to.

fields.name: artifact
fields.text: An artifact the entry involves.

label: Agent slot
summary: Adds an agent slot of the given type to a scheme.
details: Runs on a scheme. The value is the agent type, for example `agent_footpad` or `agent_muscle` in vanilla.

label: Amenity level
summary: Raises one amenity type of a character by the given value.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla uses it with `court_fashion` and `court_food_quality` and a value of 1; the documented example uses `food`.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Which amenity to raise.

fields.name: value
fields.text: How much to add.

label: Domicile building (animated)
summary: Adds a building to a domicile without cost or construction time.
details: Runs on a domicile (vanilla keys point to things like yurts and estates). The value is the domicile building key. The sibling `add_domicile_building` is documented as adding without a building animation, so this one is the variant for use with the animation.

label: Artifact history entry
summary: Adds an entry to an artifact's history, such as it being given, inherited or stolen.
details: Runs on an artifact. Vanilla uses the types `given`, `inherited`, `stolen`, `conquest` and `created`. A date is written like `624.3.13`.

fields.name: type
fields.text: What kind of event happened.
fields.values: a history entry type, for example `given` or `inherited`

fields.name: date
fields.text: When the event took place.

fields.name: actor
fields.text: Who did it, for example who created or gave the artifact.

fields.name: recipient
fields.text: Who received it, for example who the artifact was given to.

fields.name: location
fields.text: Where the event took place.

label: Artifact modifier
summary: Adds a static modifier to an artifact.
details: Runs on an artifact. The value is the name of the modifier. It cannot be given a duration.

label: Artifact title history
summary: Adds a title's history to an artifact's history, from a given date onwards.
details: Runs on an artifact. Vanilla uses it with titles such as `title:e_byzantium` and `title:d_shiite`.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The title whose history entries are taken.

fields.name: date
fields.text: The date from which entries are copied.

label: Attacker
summary: Adds the given character to a war as an attacker.
details: Runs on a war. The value is the character who joins as an attacker.

label: Barter goods
summary: Adds barter goods to a character; the game documents nothing more.

label: Building
summary: Adds a building to a province.
details: Runs on a province. The value is the building key, for example `temple_02` or `curtain_walls_01` in vanilla.

label: Character flag
summary: Puts a named flag on a character, optionally for a set time.
details: Runs on a character. A flag is a marker that scripts can check later. The short form is just a name; the long form adds a duration in days, weeks or years (vanilla also uses months). The duration can be a number or a range of two numbers, from which the game picks.

fields.name: flag
fields.text: The name of the flag.

fields.name: days
fields.text: How long the flag lasts, in days.
fields.values: a number, a range or a script value

fields.name: weeks
fields.text: How long the flag lasts, in weeks.
fields.values: a number, a range or a script value

fields.name: months
fields.text: How long the flag lasts, in months.
fields.values: a number, a range or a script value

fields.name: years
fields.text: How long the flag lasts, in years.
fields.values: a number, a range or a script value

label: Character modifier
summary: Gives a character a modifier, optionally for a set time.
details: Runs on a character. The short form is just the modifier name. The long form can add a duration in days, weeks, months or years. An optional `desc` gives the timed modifier its own description text.

fields.name: modifier
fields.text: The modifier to add.

fields.name: days
fields.text: How long it lasts, in days.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: weeks
fields.text: How long it lasts, in weeks.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: months
fields.text: How long it lasts, in months.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: years
fields.text: How long it lasts, in years.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: desc
fields.text: A dynamic description shown for the timed modifier.

label: Realm to sub-region
summary: Adds every county that is de facto part of a character's realm to a situation's sub-region.
details: Runs on a situation sub-region. The value is the character whose realm is added.

label: Clerical elector
summary: Marks a title as a clerical elector for the given faith.
details: If the title already is a clerical elector, only the faith it elects for changes. Otherwise it must be a regular title without special data and without de jure vassals. Runs on a title; the value is the faith.

label: Clerical realm to sub-region
summary: Adds every county in a clerical title's realm to a situation's sub-region.
details: Runs on a situation sub-region. The value is the clerical title.

label: Companion
summary: Adds a character as a companion on a travel plan.
details: Runs on a travel plan. The value is the character who joins the entourage.

label: Confederation member
summary: Adds a character to a confederation, unless they already belong to one.
details: The character's primary title must be of a lower tier than the confederation's title. They also become a vassal of the confederation's leader. Runs on a confederation. The documented example writes `add_member = <character>`, but vanilla writes `add_confederation_member = <character>`.

label: Confederation member house
summary: Adds a dynasty house to a confederation, unless it is already part of it.
details: Runs on a confederation. The value is the house.

label: Contact
summary: Adds the given character to the character's list of contacts.
details: Runs on a character; the value is the character who becomes a contact.

label: County modifier
summary: Gives a county a modifier, optionally for a set time.
details: Runs on a title (the county). The short form is just the modifier name. The long form can add a duration in days, weeks, months or years, and an optional `desc` as the timed modifier's description. Vanilla also uses `duration_desc`, always with `until_the_disaster_is_over`; the game's documentation does not explain it.

fields.name: modifier
fields.text: The modifier to add.

fields.name: days
fields.text: How long it lasts, in days.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: weeks
fields.text: How long it lasts, in weeks.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: months
fields.text: How long it lasts, in months.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: years
fields.text: How long it lasts, in years.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: desc
fields.text: A dynamic description shown for the timed modifier.

fields.name: duration_desc
fields.text: Not documented; vanilla only writes `until_the_disaster_is_over` here, so going by its name it is a text shown about the duration.

label: Courtier
summary: Adds the given character to the court of the character.
details: Runs on a character (the ruler whose court it is). The value is the character who joins the court.

label: Culture tradition
summary: Adds a tradition to a culture.
details: Runs on a culture. The value is the tradition, for example `tradition_horse_lords`.

label: Dead character flag
summary: Puts a named flag on a dead character for a set time.
details: A duration is required. It can be a number or a range of two numbers. Runs on a character; vanilla uses it with years.

fields.name: flag
fields.text: The name of the flag.

fields.name: years
fields.text: How long the flag lasts, in years.
fields.values: a number or a range of two numbers

fields.name: weeks
fields.text: How long the flag lasts, in weeks.
fields.values: a number or a range of two numbers

fields.name: days
fields.text: How long the flag lasts, in days.
fields.values: a number or a range of two numbers

label: Defender
summary: Adds the given character to a war as a defender.
details: Runs on a war. The value is the character who joins as a defender.

label: De jure title to sub-region
summary: Adds every county that lawfully (de jure) belongs to a title to a situation's sub-region.
details: Runs on a situation sub-region. The value is the title.

label: Advance towards the next stop
summary: Moves a travel plan forward by the given time towards its next destination.
details: Progress beyond the destination is thrown away. The on_action `on_travel_plan_movement` is not fired for any of the provinces passed, but `on_travel_plan_arrival` is fired if the destination is reached. Runs on a travel plan.

fields.name: days
fields.text: Progress in days.

fields.name: weeks
fields.text: Progress in weeks.

fields.name: months
fields.text: Progress in months.

fields.name: years
fields.text: Progress in years.

label: Diplomacy perk points
summary: Gives the character perk points in the diplomacy lifestyle.
details: Runs on a character. The game's documentation says "lifestyle per points", which reads as a typo for perk points. Vanilla almost always writes `1`.

label: Diplomacy lifestyle XP
summary: Gives the character experience in the diplomacy lifestyle.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla writes named amounts such as `minor_lifestyle_xp`, `medium_lifestyle_xp` and `major_lifestyle_xp`.

label: Diplomacy skill
summary: Adds to a character's diplomacy skill.
details: A negative amount lowers it (vanilla writes -1 and -10). The input lists no scope for this effect, but the game's documentation and the name point to a character. Vanilla mostly writes a plain number, sometimes a range like `{ 3 5 }` or a block with `value` and `subtract`.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The amount to add.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: subtract
fields.text: A script value step: vanilla's `subtract = diplomacy` takes the named skill of the character away from `value`, so the result is the amount to add. The documentation does not cover this form for the effect.

label: Doctrine
summary: Adds a doctrine to a faith.
details: Fails if the faith already has a doctrine from the same group. Runs on a faith; the value is the doctrine.

label: Domicile building
summary: Adds a building to a domicile without cost or construction time and without a building animation.
details: Runs on a domicile (vanilla keys point to things like yurts and estates). The value is the domicile building key, for example `yurt_main_02`.

label: Dread
summary: Adds dread to a character, or takes it away with a negative amount.
details: Runs on a character. Vanilla mostly uses named amounts such as `minor_dread_gain` and `medium_dread_loss`. A block form takes a `value` and a `multiply` factor.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The amount of dread.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: multiply
fields.text: A factor the value is multiplied by; vanilla uses `-1` with a cost value.
fields.values: a number or a script value

label: Durability
summary: Adds to an artifact's durability, or lowers it with a negative amount.
details: Runs on an artifact. Vanilla also writes a block with `value`, `multiply` and `max`; the game's documentation does not explain the block.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The amount to add.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: multiply
fields.text: A factor the value is multiplied by; vanilla uses values like -0.50 and 7.

fields.name: max
fields.text: Used in vanilla with numbers like 60 and with `artifact_max_durability`; going by its name, an upper limit.
fields.values: a number or a script value

label: Dynasty modifier
summary: Gives a dynasty a modifier, optionally for a set time.
details: Runs on a dynasty. The short form is just the modifier name. The long form can add a duration in days, weeks, months or years, and an optional `desc` as the timed modifier's description.

fields.name: modifier
fields.text: The modifier to add.

fields.name: days
fields.text: How long it lasts, in days.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: weeks
fields.text: How long it lasts, in weeks.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: months
fields.text: How long it lasts, in months.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: years
fields.text: How long it lasts, in years.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: desc
fields.text: A dynamic description shown for the timed modifier.

label: Legacy (dynasty perk)
summary: Gives a dynasty a dynasty perk (a legacy).
details: Runs on a dynasty. The value is the perk key, for example `warfare_legacy_1`.
